entries.title: Week 7: preserve the better early draft and the missed assumptions
entries.question: Did the anticipated opportunity appear, and what explains the final team's result versus earlier drafts?
entries.why_it_matters: A later draft can score worse even when some new role checks are sound. Preserve the whole trajectory rather than judging only the final nine.
findings: The frozen nine reconstruct to 114.22; Tuesday and Wednesday each 129.52. These are provisional under the inspected DraftKings rules.
Nabers: nine targets, seven catches, 111 yards with McCarthy starting. St. Brown: 11 targets, nine catches, 153 yards.
Kittle: ten targets, eight catches, 88 yards and one lost fumble. Marks: 19 carries, but just one receiving target.
Godwin: five of 11 team targets; Tampa Bay ran 49 times. Quarterback availability and target share did not establish a large passing opportunity.
LaPorta: two targets; Keenan: three targets in 22 Colts attempts. Pollard had 25 carries/three targets; Braelon 17 carries/seven targets.
entries.interpretation: The Nabers, St. Brown, Kittle and Marks role claims largely held within their stated limits. The result still exposed weak absolute volume and concentrated target competition. Tuesday's higher score must remain visible; neither it nor the final score alone proves better reasoning.
alternatives: Pollard's original workload choice remained defensible; his three touchdowns amplified the result, so do not forecast that score forward.
The last St. Brown/Kittle package gained 15.10 over Puka/Keenan, while earlier RB changes lost 30.40 from Pollard to Marks.
Claude's separate original reconstructs to 102.92; this is not a controlled comparison or an author ranking.
uncertainty: Platform settlement and later stat corrections are unverified.
Routes, snaps and all final inactive lists were not retrieved; mechanisms beyond inspected targets/carries remain unassessable.
In-game CMC injury changed conditions; it cannot be retroactively incorporated into pregame reasoning.
entries.lineup_effect: No selection edits after freeze. Add only provisional actuals to the display view, retaining all original salaries, rationales, estimates and cutoffs.
change_triggers: Append a correction only for materially changed verified scoring inputs or platform evidence.
Reassess carried lessons when fresh prices, availability and role evidence differ.
carry_forward: Compare absolute team passing volume with target share; a healthy-enough quarterback and a large share can coexist with a small passing pie.
Separate rushing role from touchdown outcome and receiving floor; Marks led carries while Pollard and Braelon had much stronger scoring results.
Treat same-team receiver/TE competition as a whole-lineup concentration risk; one game is a provisional lesson, not a rule.

entries.title: Week 8 starts unpriced: investigate Detroit allocation and RB opportunity
entries.question: Which observed roles deserve price-sensitive investigation on the November 1 slate?
entries.why_it_matters: The new slate removes five frozen selections through byes/Thursday scheduling. Reusing old salaries would create a false budget solution.
findings: Primary NFL schedule lists 11 Sunday-afternoon candidate games on November 1; earliest at 13:00 ET. The actual DraftKings game set remains unverified.
The inspected Week 8 salary page explicitly has no posted prices. No official export or sufficiently priced lineup was established in the bounded pass.
Williams had nine targets alongside St. Brown's 11; LaPorta had two. Williams is a candidate beyond the prior nine.
Irving carried 24 times, but his team ran 49 times and Gainwell carried 14. Braelon had 17 carries/seven targets; Pollard 25/three.
entries.interpretation: Begin with an unpriced board. Test whether roles persist, then compare the entire salary package. Williams and Irving warrant discovery work without assuming their touchdowns or favorable scripts repeat.
alternatives: LaPorta may become attractive at a sufficiently low new price, but a high team scoring environment is not proof of his individual target volume.
Retain Godwin and Keenan as questions rather than automatic selections; new team volume, health and price can change their cases.
uncertainty: Actual DraftKings main-slate identity, game membership, eligible player IDs, positions and current salaries.
Week 8 availability reports and a coherent optional external projection snapshot.
Whether the observed workload conditions persist: Hall, Mayfield, Detroit competition and game script.
No numerical whole-lineup price tradeoff can be performed before verified prices.
entries.lineup_effect: Zero priced picks; $0 allocated and $50,000 unallocated. Projections null. Partial board cannot be frozen or announced as codex_v1_ready.
change_triggers: A real official salary export or sufficient attributable selected prices, linked to the actual main slate.
Current availability and role evidence establishing whether the observed carry/target opportunity persists.
A supported alternative package that improves the whole roster under the cap; no forced churn.
carry_forward: Check Hall and the Jets backfield split before projecting Braelon's observed role forward.
Check Mayfield's throwing condition and Tampa Bay's likely passing volume, not only whether he can play.
Preserve Codex's first supported complete Week 8 v1 before inspecting another author's picks where feasible; a partial board does not unlock downstream stages.
November 1 local cutoff is 12:30 Toronto / 17:30 UTC because daylight saving time ends.
